body:
## Problem

`nvim_set_option_value()` dry runs skip checks in `did_set_*` callbacks, so they can accept values that assignments reject. This logic also prepares values needed to apply the option, such as tab widths or a compiled regexp. Moving the checks into validation callbacks needs a way to save that work for `did_set_*`.

## Solution

Store prepared values in `optset_T` so `did_set_*` can consume them after the option is stored. Dry runs perform the same validation, then free the prepared values without changing live state.

This extends dry-run validation for:

- `cedit`: reject invalid command-line window keys.
- `completeitemalign`: require each completion column exactly once.
- `cursorlineopt`: reject empty values and conflicting line modes.
- `encoding`: accept only UTF-8 and its aliases.
- `fileencoding`: reject lists and local changes with `nomodifiable`.
- `messagesopt`: require mandatory fields and enforce numeric limits.
- `spellcapcheck`: return regexp errors, including under `:silent!`.
- `spellsuggest`: reject conflicting suggestion modes.
- `varsofttabstop` and `vartabstop`: reject invalid tab widths.
- `wildmode`: reject more than four completion stages.

`makeencoding` also uses the shared encoding preparation.

Separating value preparation exposed a bug in `vartabstop` and `varsofttabstop`: failed assignments could discard local tab widths, and global assignments could overwrite them. Fix this by preparing new widths separately and applying them only after a valid local assignment.

comment_data.body: AIs love to create new special-purpose structs

I did review this.

What would be more preferable? A `prepared_data` and `prepared_free` fields in `optset_T`?

I personally don't mind having special purpose structs. It's no different to all the `@class`s we have in Lua.

Hmm, we need to pass `OptPrepared` to `did_set_option` which already has 11 arguments. Removing this struct would take it to 12 arguments, so I think we probably need to keep it.

Separately I noticed a bunch of functions (~19) taking `char *errbuf, size_t errbuflen`, and it might be worth combining these into a struct.

1. Abort state leaks out of a failed compile. When the wrapped compile reports an error, `cause_errthrow()` sets `cause_abort = true`. `try_leave()` resets `force_abort` but not `cause_abort`. Normally `do_errthrow()` consumes it at the end of a nested command, but there is no nested command here, so it stays set until the next command boundary and turns into `force_abort` there. The result: a script that runs `lua pcall(vim.api.nvim_set_option_value, 'spellcapcheck', [[\(]], {dry_run=true})` and then hits any ordinary error, such as `call NoSuchFunc()`, is aborted instead of continuing. A failed API assignment that isn't a dry run leaks the flag the same way.
2. `:silent!` can stop working. `emsg_silent` is forced to 0 so that `TRY_WRAP` collects the error. But `cause_errthrow()` skips collection while `suppress_errthrow` is set: after an uncaught error until the next top-level `do_cmdline()` (`ex_docmd.c:816`/`:937`), and inside `assert_fails()`/`assert_beeps()`. In those cases E54 goes through the normal `emsg()` path: it is displayed and stored in `v:errmsg`, and the caller gets a generic E474 instead of E54. That is the "no message-state change" behaviour the new tests assert.

Both bugs come from writing error capture by hand inside one option's validator. A shared "compile a pattern and return its error text" helper would fix both, and `vim.regex` could use it too.

`did_set_cursorlineopt()` copies a `:setglobal culopt=…` value into the current window's flags. `:setlocal culopt=both | setglobal culopt=number` stops the cursorline in that window, while `:setlocal culopt?` still says `both`.

This bug is present on master but this PR fixes it for `'vartabstop'`/`'varsofttabstop'`/`'spellcapcheck'` with an `os_varp == &p_xx` guard, that just got missed here.
(also present on master) Clearing `'vartabstop'` doesn't recompute indent folds: the `*array != NULL` condition skips `foldUpdateAll()`.

This PR uses two patterns for the same job. `'completeitemalign'` and `'cursorlineopt'` pass parsed flags from validation to `did_set_*` through `os_prepared.flags`, while `'wildmode'` and `'spellsuggest'` use one parser with an
optional output and re-parse in `did_set_*`. Re-parsing is trivial here, so suggest using the second pattern everywhere and dropping `os_prepared.flags`; `os_prepared` then only carries results that allocate or are expensive to build
(regexp, tab-stop arrays, encoding). As a side effect, `did_set_cursorlineopt()` re-parsing `win->w_p_culopt` would no longer apply a `:setglobal` value to the current window (item 3). The `return e_invarg` branches left in
`did_set_wildmode()`/`did_set_spellsuggest()` can then go, since they re-parse a value that was just validated.

I don't think separate it()'s are needed for these, they can be one `it('dry-run does not have side-effects')`.

Overuse of it() is rather noisy in the test results.

comment_data.body:
> This PR uses two patterns for the same job. 'completeitemalign' and 'cursorlineopt' pass parsed flags from validation to did_set_* through os_prepared.flags, while 'wildmode' and 'spellsuggest' use one parser with an
optional output and re-parse in did_set_*. Re-parsing is trivial here, so suggest using the second pattern everywhere and dropping os_prepared.flags; os_prepared then only carries results that allocate or are expensive to build
(regexp, tab-stop arrays, encoding).

`flags` was added for specific cases to avoid needing to allocate and providing a free function. It could be removed, but will likely increase code. I personally think it's worth keeping since there's enough options that do (or could) use it.

> As a side effect, did_set_cursorlineopt() re-parsing win->w_p_culopt would no longer apply a :setglobal value to the current window (item 3). 

This is a pre-existing problem before this PR. I can fix it here but is AI-bug-fixing creep.

> The return e_invarg branches left in
did_set_wildmode()/did_set_spellsuggest() can then go, since they re-parse a value that was just validated.

Those branches existed before this PR but can be removed now.
I guess freeing a pointer that has been cleared is a fair enough convention.
Since you've mentioned it, I'll fix it.

> Abort state leaks out of a failed compile.

I could not reproduce the script abort with the stated sequence. Both dry runs and assignments continued after `call NoSuchFunc()`. `do_errthrow()` consumes `cause_abort`, then the command loop clears `force_abort` after the successful `:lua` command. Could you share the exact script or call context?

> `:silent!` can stop working.

Confirmed inside `assert_fails()` and `assert_nobeep()`. E54 is displayed and changes `v:errmsg`, while `pcall` receives E474. Clearing `emsg_silent` does not ensure error capture when `suppress_errthrow` is set. This needs a fix and a regression test.

> A shared … helper would fix both

A shared helper may make sense, but it must fix the error-capture behaviour. Moving the existing `TRY_WRAP` into a helper would preserve the problem. I would separate that design choice from the confirmed bug above.
